summary: The rule pays one and one-half times the base rate on every hour of the question (8 hours -> 716.16). The clause pays that premium only for hours worked in excess of the regularly scheduled hours in a single day, or of 40 hours in a week for part-time employees; the roster has no scheduled-hours fact, so the rule treats every hour asked about as overtime. The MOU never defines regular rate of pay, and the 2.5% longevity increase on p.5 is not in the rate the rule multiplies. Every number here came from the engine.

warnings.claim: The rule fires whenever hours > 0 and pays 1.5x on all of them. The cited clause pays the premium only for hours worked in excess of the regularly scheduled hours worked in a single day, or in excess of 40 hours in a week for employees working less than 40 hours. A 4-hour entry pays 358.08 as written, although the clause would pay nothing unless those hours exceeded the day's schedule; the engine rejected a variant conditioned on the scheduled hours as an unknown fact.

evidence.quote: Employees shall be compensated at the rate of one and one-half times their regular rate of pay for all hours worked in excess of:
Any time over the regularly scheduled hours worked in a single day.
For employees working less than 40 hours, any hours worked in excess of 40 hours in a week.

counter_example.why: 8 hours pays 716.16 and 4 hours pays 358.08 as written; both assume every hour asked about is already past the regularly scheduled hours. The clause gives no premium for the scheduled hours themselves, and the data holds no scheduled-hours or hours-this-week fact to apply the threshold.

warnings.suggested_action: State in the answer that the hours are taken to be beyond the regular schedule; add a scheduled-hours fact before the rule can apply the trigger itself.

warnings.claim: The clause multiplies the employee's regular rate of pay. The rule multiplies the salary-schedule base rate. This MOU does not define regular rate of pay: a search for the definition returned only the overtime clause itself, the Definitions heading on p.11 and the grievance definition on p.18. The education incentive on p.5 ($300.00 a month for a Bachelor's Degree) is additional pay the rule does not consider.

Bachelor's Degree: shall receive $ 300.00 a month as incentive pay.

warnings.suggested_action: Have the analyst record which items the District includes in the regular rate for this unit; until then the answer should say the base rate was used.

warnings.claim: Page 5 grants a 2.5% pay increase upon completion of ten (10) years of service, and another 2.5% at twenty (20) years. The rule multiplies the top-step base rate with no service fact. With the ten-year increase in the rate an 8-hour overtime shift pays 734.06 instead of 716.16.

evidence.quote: Upon completion of ten (10) years of service to the District an employee shall receive a 2.5% pay increase.
Upon completion of twenty (20) years of service to the District employees shall receive a 2.5% pay increase calculated from their date of hire.

counter_example.why: 8 hours at the top-step base rate pays 716.16 as written; with the 2.5% ten-year longevity increase folded into the rate the same shift pays 734.06. The roster has no years-of-service fact.

warnings.suggested_action: Add a years-of-service fact to the roster and a longevity differential rule; the answer should state that longevity is not included.

warnings.claim: Overtime compensation is accumulated in one-half (1/2) hour increments; the rule pays any fraction. An 8.25-hour entry pays 738.54 as written and 716.16 when the hours are rounded to the half hour.

evidence.quote: Overtime compensation shall be accumulated in one-half (1/2) hour increments.

counter_example.why: 8.25 hours pays 738.54 as written; rounded to the nearest half hour the engine returns 716.16. The clause never pays a quarter hour.

warnings.suggested_action: Round hours to the half hour before multiplying, or refuse a fractional entry that is not a half-hour multiple.

warnings.claim: The rule always returns a dollar amount. With supervisor approval an administrative employee may receive earned overtime as compensatory time off, up to an 80-hour bank; only hours beyond the 80-hour maximum are paid out at the overtime rate.

evidence.quote: Administrative employees are eligible to receive earned overtime in the form of compensatory time off with the approval of their supervisor.
